identity.title: POCUS cardiac: RV dilation (RV:LV >1), septal flattening, McConnell sign

technique.how: Phased-array probe. In the apical 4-chamber view compare RV to LV end-diastolic basal diameter (RV:LV >1 = dilated; >0.6-0.9 mild); in parasternal short axis look for a flattened or D-shaped septum bowing into the LV; assess RV free-wall motion for akinesis with preserved apical contraction (McConnell sign). Confirm in subcostal view if apical window is poor.
technique.prerequisites: Adequate apical or subcostal window; trained operator; compare with prior echo if available to separate acute from chronic RV disease.

interpretation.positive_finding: RV dilation (RV:LV >1) identified by emergency physicians is highly specific for PE in moderate/high-probability patients (specificity 98%, LR+ 29); McConnell sign and paradoxical septal motion were seen only in patients with PE in that cohort.
interpretation.negative_finding: A normal RV does not exclude PE (sensitivity ~50% for RV dilation, 53% for pooled 'right heart strain'; LR- 0.5); it argues against a hemodynamically significant (massive/submassive) PE as the cause of shock.
interpretation.pitfalls: Chronic pulmonary hypertension, COPD/cor pulmonale, RV infarction, and ARDS/high PEEP also dilate the RV; foreshortened apical views under- or over-estimate RV size. Sensitivity and specificity in low-probability, unselected dyspneic patients are lower than in the enriched cohorts.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: in suspected PE treat as high-risk PE (CTPA if stable, consider thrombolysis if unstable); negative: PE not excluded, continue pretest-probability-driven work-up.

estimates.target_condition: Pulmonary embolism (finding: undefined 'right heart strain' on transthoracic echo)
estimates.population: Patients with suspected PE across included diagnostic-accuracy studies (systematic review through 2016); mixed operators including cardiologists and emergency physicians
estimates.reference_standard: CT pulmonary angiography, V/Q scan, or conventional angiography (study-specific)
estimates.quote: it had a sensitivity of 53% (95% CI, 45%-61%) and a specificity of 83% (95% CI, 74%-90%)

estimates.target_condition: Pulmonary embolism (finding: RV dilatation, RV:LV ratio >1:1, on emergency-physician bedside echo)
estimates.population: ED convenience sample of 146 patients with suspected (moderate-high pretest probability) or confirmed PE; 30 had PE
estimates.reference_standard: Final radiology reading of CT pulmonary angiography or other definitive imaging plus chart review
estimates.quote: sensitivity of 50% (95% confidence interval [CI] 32% to 68%), a specificity of 98% (95% CI 95% to 100%)

sources.citation: Fields JM, Davis J, Girson L, et al. Transthoracic echocardiography for diagnosing pulmonary embolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Am Soc Echocardiogr. 2017;30(7):714-723.e4.

Dresden S, Mitchell P, Rahimi L, et al. Right ventricular dilatation on bedside echocardiography performed by emergency physicians aids in the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism. Ann Emerg Med. 2014;63(1):16-24.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a normal RV to exclude PE in a stable patient; do not attribute RV dilation to PE without considering chronic pulmonary hypertension or RV infarction, especially when the RV free wall is thickened.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: RV dilation with hypotension in suspected PE indicates high-risk PE: activate PE response/ICU and consider systemic thrombolysis or catheter/surgical embolectomy.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Dresden 2014 reported 96% observed agreement between co-investigators and the principal investigator on recorded images; pooled 'right heart strain' definitions varied widely across studies (Fields 2017).
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency physician or intensivist with focused cardiac ultrasound training capable of obtaining apical 4-chamber and parasternal short-axis views; Dresden 2014 operators were ED physicians with ultrasound credentialing.

extraction_notes: Fields 2017 abstract supplies only the pooled 'right heart strain' estimate; sign-specific pooled values (RV:LV ratio, McConnell, septal motion, 60/60) are in the article tables, which were not accessible (no PMC), so they are not entered. Dresden 2014 LR+ 29 (95% CI 6.1-64) and LR- 0.51 (0.4-0.7) are as reported in the abstract (the abstract's '%' after CI bounds is a typographical artefact); McConnell sign (6/6) and paradoxical septal motion (8/8) were 100% specific but too few for sensitivity, noted qualitatively. Prevalence 0.205 computed from 30/146. Population is enriched for moderate-high pretest probability; expect lower PPV in unselected dyspnea.
